evidenceAudit.scope: Adults receiving anticancer treatment with suspected neutropenic sepsis: emergency assessment, immediate empiric therapy and risk-led disposition using NICE CG151.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national neutropenic-sepsis protocol was opened.
The title's one-hour target is a local operational goal; NICE CG151 says immediately but does not state one hour in the recommendation.
Piperacillin-tazobactam dose, allergy alternative and SFDA registration require the hospital antimicrobial protocol.

pathophysiology.summary: Anticancer treatment can suppress neutrophil production and innate immune defence. Infection may progress rapidly with muted local inflammatory signs. Bacterial translocation and device-related infection are common potential sources. Sepsis causes vasodilation, endothelial injury and organ hypoperfusion.
keyMechanisms: Anticancer treatment can suppress neutrophil production and innate immune defence.
Infection may progress rapidly with muted local inflammatory signs.
Bacterial translocation and device-related infection are common potential sources.
Sepsis causes vasodilation, endothelial injury and organ hypoperfusion.

symptoms: Fever, chills, malaise, confusion, breathlessness, urinary or GI symptoms, or simply feeling unwell during anticancer treatment.
physicalSigns: Temperature above 38°C, hypotension, tachycardia, altered mental state, hypoxia or focal infection signs; fever may be absent.
redFlags: Shock, lactate elevation, altered consciousness, respiratory failure, oliguria or rapidly deteriorating physiology.
precipitants: Recent chemotherapy or radiotherapy, central venous access device, mucositis and prior resistant organism.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Same emergency physiology but neutrophil count above the diagnostic threshold; treat sepsis without delay.
Diagnosis of exclusion after immediate empiric treatment and assessment.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirms neutropenia but treatment starts on suspicion without waiting.
ruleIn.normalValue: Neutrophils above 0.5 × 10^9/L for this diagnostic criterion

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Collect promptly without delaying empiric antibiotics; lactate informs resuscitation/escalation.
ruleIn.normalValue: No growth; lactate within local reference range

ruleIn.targetCondition: Sepsis organ dysfunction and antibiotic dosing
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Acute kidney injury or electrolyte disturbance
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Guide resuscitation and local-protocol antimicrobial dosing.
ruleIn.normalValue: Within local adult laboratory reference range

ruleIn.targetCondition: Sepsis organ dysfunction or treatment toxicity
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Establish baseline and guide treatment review.
ruleIn.normalValue: Within local adult laboratory reference range

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use as one trend alongside physiology and microbiology; a low value does not exclude early neutropenic sepsis.
Collect before antibiotics when this causes no delay; tailor treatment with microbiology.
Obtain an additional peripheral culture when a central line is present and it is clinically feasible.
ruleIn.normalValue: No growth from line or peripheral samples

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Chest, urine, line, skin, oral and GI sources
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Do not obtain routine chest X-ray unless clinically indicated.

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Pulmonary infection or alternative thoracic cause
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Focal infiltrate or other acute abnormality
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Do not perform routinely; request only for respiratory signs or another clinical indication.

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and escalate
actions: Treat any unwell patient receiving anticancer treatment as suspected neutropenic sepsis until assessed.
Begin sepsis resuscitation, obtain cultures and core blood tests without delaying antibiotics.

clinicalManagement.title: Start empiric antibiotic
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Immediately; local operational target within 1 hour
actions: Give IV piperacillin-tazobactam monotherapy unless patient-specific allergy, microbiology or local resistance factors require another regimen.
Do not add an aminoglycoside or glycopeptide routinely without a patient-specific or microbiological indication.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm diagnosis and risk
actions: Confirm using neutrophil count and fever or significant sepsis features.
A competent oncology clinician uses a validated risk score and clinical/social context to determine inpatient versus outpatient therapy.

clinicalManagement.title: Daily review and step-down
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Daily; consider oral switch after 48 hours only if reassessed low risk
actions: Do not switch solely for persistent fever unless deterioration or microbiology indicates.
Discharge only after competent low-risk reassessment, stable circumstances and explicit rapid-return instructions.

medicationPlan.note: NICE CG151 selects piperacillin-tazobactam IV monotherapy but does not specify the dose. Use the Saudi hospital antimicrobial protocol for dose, renal adjustment, allergy alternative and infusion method.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Anticancer treatment plus neutrophil count 0.5 × 10^9/L or lower and temperature above 38°C, or other clinically significant sepsis features.

teaching.scope: Adults receiving anticancer treatment with suspected neutropenic sepsis: emergency assessment, immediate empiric therapy and risk-led disposition using NICE CG151.
learningObjectives: Recognise neutropenic sepsis before the count returns.
Deliver immediate empiric therapy and risk-led disposition.
pitfalls: Waiting for neutrophil count or imaging before antibiotics.
Treating persistent fever alone as automatic antibiotic failure.
keyPoints: The NICE diagnostic neutrophil threshold is 0.5 × 10^9/L or lower.
Routine aminoglycoside or glycopeptide addition is not recommended.

patientEducation: Give oncology emergency contact instructions and advise immediate return for any deterioration.
lifestyleAndDiet: Follow oncology infection-prevention advice; do not delay care to self-manage fever.
mdtReferrals: Acute oncology/haematology, infectious diseases or microbiology, pharmacy and critical care.
dischargeCriteria: Only after competent low-risk reassessment, clinical stability, suitable social circumstances and rapid return access.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Daily specialist reassessment while high risk; outpatient follow-up frequency is set by the oncology team and local protocol.
